canonicalExplanation.summary: Physical properties (`margin-left`, `padding-right`, `left`) stay on the same side of the screen whatever the language. **Logical properties** follow the text direction instead: `margin-inline-start` is the left in English but the right in Arabic or Hebrew; `block` means the direction lines stack (top to bottom in most languages). Set `dir="rtl"` on the HTML and logical layouts mirror automatically.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Your course site launches in Arabic. You set `dir="rtl"` and `text-align: right` — the text flips, but icons still sit on the left of labels, indents point the wrong way, and the card's accent border is on the wrong side. RTL isn't just text alignment. A card uses margin-inline-start instead of margin-left, so spacing mirrors in right-to-left text. In this lesson you'll refactor directional properties and verify a component in left-to-right and right-to-left contexts.

```predict
{"question": "In an RTL page, where is `margin-inline-start` applied?", "options": ["On the left", "On the right — the start side of right-to-left text"], "answer": 1, "why": "Inline-start is where lines of text begin: left in LTR, right in RTL."}
```

outcomes: Refactor directional properties and verify a component in left-to-right and right-to-left contexts.

examples.title: A card that mirrors in Arabic
examples.situation: A card uses margin-inline-start instead of margin-left so spacing mirrors in right-to-left text.
walkthrough: **Before:** `border-left`, `margin-left`, `text-align: left` — correct in English, wrong in Arabic.
**Verify:** set `dir="rtl"` on the page; the browser will render the accent border, indent and icon gap on the right, mirroring the LTR card.
examples.result: One stylesheet produces correct cards in both English and Arabic.

examples.title: The half-mirrored form
examples.situation: A form under `dir="rtl"` has right-aligned labels, but error icons still sit on the left and the input's padding leaves the text cramped on the right.
walkthrough: Only text-align was changed; spacing still uses physical properties.
The input's `padding-left` should be on the start side.
Fix: `padding-inline-start` and `margin-inline-end` for icons; test with real Arabic text.
examples.result: The form mirrors completely, with comfortable spacing on the correct sides.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: RTL support is complete when text-align is switched to right.
misconceptions.correction: Right-to-left layouts need spacing, borders, positions and directional icons to mirror too. Logical properties do this automatically once the document direction is set.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The half-mirrored form", what was still wrong after aligning text right?

analogy.example: Logical properties are like saying **"at the start of the queue"** instead of **"on the left"**. If the queue turns around (RTL), "start" still means the right place, while "left" now points to the back.
limitations: Queues rarely turn; languages on one site often do.
Some icons, like a clock, don't turn with the queue.

steps.explanation: A card uses margin-inline-start instead of margin-left.
In left-to-right text, the start side is the left.
In right-to-left text the spacing mirrors automatically.

trace.textAlternative: One card in two directions. Step 1, Refactor: margin-left is → margin-inline-start. A card uses margin-inline-start instead of margin-left. Step 2, LTR: border is left; margin is left. In left-to-right text, the start side is the left. Step 3, RTL: border is right; margin is right. In right-to-left text the spacing mirrors automatically.

nearTransfer.prompt: Convert: `.note { padding-left: 1rem; border-right: 2px solid; text-align: left; margin-top: 1rem; }`.

farTransfer.prompt: Refactor one component's stylesheet to logical properties, add `dir="rtl"` test page with real Arabic or Hebrew text, and compare screenshots side by side.
expectedEvidence: No physical left/right properties remain (except deliberate ones).

remediation.explanation: Search your CSS for `left` and `right`. For each, ask: **Should this follow the reading direction?** If yes, switch to inline-start/end. Then test with dir="rtl".

recap.summary: To refactor directional properties, replace left/right with inline-start/end and top/bottom with block-start/end, set dir in HTML, mirror directional icons, and verify the component in both left-to-right and right-to-left contexts.
